title: Fit a line by least squares
instructions:
## What .fit() computes

For points (x, y) the least-squares line has slope `b = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ) / Σ(x−x̄)²` and intercept `a = ȳ − b·x̄`.

## Do this

1. `fit_line(xs, ys)` returns `(slope, intercept)` as a tuple.
2. `predict(model, x)` returns `slope * x + intercept` for a model tuple.
3. `r_squared(xs, ys)` returns 1 − SSres/SStot, where SSres is the sum of squared residuals of the fitted line and SStot the sum of squared deviations of y from its mean.

Use plain Python; no numpy.
